resolutions.finding: must_fix (report): Omitted item 1 misdescribed code's dominance and missed that gamma's dominance over beta holds inside the bars.
resolutions.evidence: Removed from Omitted. Method 'Bars as the condition' now states it the way options_dominance has it: gamma dominates beta, beta dominates alpha, each on cost with answering not separated, and gamma does not dominate alpha, which is ahead of it (+4.6 to +74.2, matching aspects.answers.pair.alpha.gamma.interval). The gamma why_not says the pipeline's dominance reading favours gamma over beta, and the recommendation says why the report ranks answering above that cost tie-break.

resolutions.finding: should_fix (report): the pick departs from the campaign kind's rule (a pick shown ahead on no pair rests on cost or simplicity) without saying so; move the 8.1% wrong-side figure into the recommendation.
resolutions.evidence: The recommendation now names the rule, says it would choose gamma, and gives the reason for departing (the question ranks answering inside the bars). The 8.1% figure stays in Watch, and Method 'Rerun risk' says why: it assumes today's gap is the true one, so it sizes a rerun's risk rather than evidencing the lead. That is a sound reason to decline the second half of the suggestion.

resolutions.finding: should_fix (c3): the scoreboard block did not show the settle sizing (240 against 60) or the wrong-side rate.
resolutions.evidence: The settle claim and its scoreboard block are gone. The 240 and 8.1% sit in What settles it, Watch and Next step 1, read through settle.* keys. An Omitted entry says no block draws the settle sizing. The old c4 is now c3.

resolutions.evidence: What settles it and Next step 1 now say fresh cases, the same for both arms, at today's {repeats|int} (3) repeats each, and 'Repeating today's {cases|int} cases more often does not count toward it.' settle_cases confirms the count is trials (spread n = 60, counts = trials, basis = each arm's stated interval). 240 matches today's case-based spread scaled from 60 trials, so it means about 80 fresh cases at 3 repeats.

resolutions.finding: should_fix (report): the minimum-answer-rate control read the floor on point estimates while bars are read on intervals.
resolutions.evidence: The explore outcome now gives both readings. On the estimates, a floor between 45% and 65% leaves beta alone. On whole intervals, no floor separates beta from gamma, because their intervals overlap. Next step 2 asks the owner to declare which reading applies.

resolutions.evidence: It is now bounded: '... but stays above gamma's (373.3 ms to 428.7 ms) leaves gamma the only arm inside; below gamma's, no arm qualifies.' The cost-bar control right next to it still has the same unbounded form (new finding).

resolutions.evidence: A scan of every prose field outside braces finds no typed numerals or number words other than unit labels ('Cost per 1,000 replies', p95). The three phrases are gone.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline says what to do (beta, provisionally) and the main risk (it cannot be separated from the cheaper gamma). The decision block gives the why: 65% against 45%, both inside the $1.00-per-1,000 and 800 ms bars, alpha out on both at $4.00 and 1001 ms. It also gives the fallback: if the +20-point lead (-9.3 to +47.6) is noise, gamma is the pick. c1 shows the bar verdicts with budget lines. Watch adds the nearest line: turn time 99 ms under the bar on the mean, p95 791.6 ms.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (bars rule alpha out) leads to c2 (inside the bars beta leads gamma, unseparated) and then c3 (every failure is a wrong total). The recommendation now names its departure from the kind's cost rule and from code's dominance, both of which pick gamma, and gives its reason. Nothing contradicts the headline. One internal inconsistency in how the bars are read (mean in Watch and Omitted, whole interval in Explore) is noted below. It does not touch the c1 verdict, since alpha misses and beta and gamma clear on either reading.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Beta's weak points are on the first screen: its lead is unseparated in the headline, lede, recommendation and c2; gamma is cheaper and faster (gamma why_not); turn time is its nearest line, with p95 791.6 ms against an 800 ms bar. Confidence is low with all 17 caveats open. Alpha's unseparated lead over beta (-7.1 to +39.3) is stated. The bare imperative 'Use {arm:beta}.' at the start of the recommendation is qualified two sentences later and in the headline.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: The omissions check out against the snapshot. The unpaired beta-gamma interval (-0.080 to +0.480) gives the same verdict as the corrected one. The unpaired alpha-beta interval just clears zero (+0.00065), but alpha is out on the bars. Production cost equals spend. The 9 frozen failures carry no excerpt, input or expected total (examples_list). A turn-time threshold sweep moves no option in code's reading, because bars only warn there. The weakest omission is price per point: its reason is a unit conversion ($1.50 per whole unit is $0.015 per 1,000 replies per point), and the cost gap behind it (+$0.30 per 1,000 replies) is never stated in prose. The c1 block shows $0.80 and $0.50, so the reader can still see it.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All 17 snapshot caveats appear, each with a material_if clause. best_of_n and nothing_declared carry into the lede, the decision and Next steps 1 and 2. ingest_backlog gets its own Next step 3, and its clause names the real risk: a backlog would move turn time and answer rate together, which is exactly the gap between gamma and beta. The orchestration_ms gap is explained as not bearing on a whole-turn bar. The no_control clause is the loosest: 'not reverse the bar verdicts' is beside the point, since the bars are absolute and pairing cannot touch them.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Step 1 is a sized experiment: fresh shared cases, 3 repeats, about 240 trials per arm (about 80 cases). It is consistent with settle_cases, and it says what happens if the lead is not real. Step 2 is a declaration: a minimum answer rate and how it is read. Step 3 records the apparatus, backlog first. Step 4 (compare failing cases) is diagnostic rather than decisive, but it says what each outcome would mean.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c1's two bars blocks with budget lines fit, and the counterfactual holds. So does c3's per-arm table: a cites_policy rate below 1 would break the claim. c2 is a lead claim, and its decisive figure has no block: the corrected pair gap (-9.3 to +47.6 at 98%). The dot_interval shows each arm's own 95% interval, a different statistic at a different level. If the pair interval cleared zero while the own intervals still overlapped, the block would not change and the claim would. The claim now says so, which makes it honest but not the clearest evidence. c3's headers also print raw measure keys.

findings.finding: The bars are read on two different statistics. The criteria declare statistic: mean, and code reads beta's turn time at 701 ms (criteria.answers/bar/total_ms.beta.value). Watch ('99 ms under the bar on its mean') and Omitted ('The bar reads the mean') follow that. But the turn-time explore control has a bar that 'cuts into' beta's interval removing beta, and the floor control says 'Read on whole intervals, as the bars are'. For a turn-time bar between 701 and 728.7 ms the two readings disagree about beta. Pick one reading and make Explore follow it. If the report deliberately reads stricter than the declared mean, say so once in Method.

The cost-bar explore control has the flaw round 1 fixed in the turn-time one. 'Lowering the bar under {scoreboard.beta.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} leaves {arm:gamma} the only arm inside' is wrong under gamma's own $0.50 per 1,000 replies, where no arm qualifies. Bound it the same way.

The size of the saving the report declines is never stated in prose. The recommendation overrides both the kind's cost rule and code's dominance, and nothing_declared leaves the trade to the owner, so the owner needs that size: beta costs {price.gamma.beta.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.cost_gap|usd_per_1k} (+$0.30 per 1,000 replies) more than gamma. Put it in the gamma why_not. The Omitted reason for dropping price per point is a unit conversion, not a reason to omit it.

The lead claim's decisive figure, the corrected pair gap at 98%, still has no block. The dot_interval shows each arm's own 95% spread. If the kit has a difference or contrast block that can draw a pair reading with its corrected interval, use it here. If it has none, record that as a gap rather than leaving the caption to carry it.

The no_control material_if ends with 'not reverse the bar verdicts', which is beside the point: the bars are absolute and no pairing touches them. The caveat's real reach is that nothing is read paired, so beta against gamma rests on each arm's own spread. Say that a paired read over the shared cases could separate them, which would firm the pick and shrink the 240-trial sizing, or could leave them unseparated.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 5: the c3 table's column headers print the measure keys 'reply.cites_policy' and 'reply.total == case.total' above the appendix (blocks.txt c3/1). The snapshot's display names for these measures are those same keys, so the fix is likely a display name in the campaign or the renderer rather than in the document.

Invariant 5: one caveat id carries internal measure names, 'unreported:orchestration_ms (llm_ms, tool_ms were not measured ...)'. If the page prints caveat ids rather than display labels in the confidence section, those names reach the page.
Invariant 6: Method is present. The report-doc has no full-results appendix field, so this could not be verified from the document.

Invariants 1-4 hold: all 27 cited figure keys read on the snapshot (figure_keys_check, none refused or unstated), no typed numbers remain in prose, all 17 caveats appear with material_if, and the confidence form is low with caveats open.
